result.summary:
Independently re-read docs/requirements.yaml's REQ-038 entry (lines 1778-1820, 5 acceptance criteria verbatim), lib/letflow/design/req038-promotion-rollback.md in full (including §0's Rework-1 evidence and §6/§7's exactly-one-match safe default), lib/letflow/definitions.ex's rollback_definition_version/4 plus its 5 private helpers (do_rollback/6, run_rollback_transaction/4, swap_active_pointer/3, finish_rollback/8, supersede_matching_review/4) directly against the shipped code, and promotion_review_store.ex's widened supersede_review/3 (confirmed allowed_source_statuses is literally [:applied, :approved, :failed, :rejected], moduledoc updated to 'Exactly 8 permitted edges'). Read test/specs/REQ-038.md and test/letflow/definitions/rollback_test.exs in full, not just TEST-DESIGNER's summary.

All 5 acceptance criteria have unambiguous runnable coverage: AC1 (2 tests, full success-path incl. exactly-one-event proof via refute_receive, plus get_active_by_name/2 queryable-state parity), AC2 (3 tests: draft-never-activated with updated_at pinning, no-row-at-all, archived-excluded per INV-RB-4), AC3 (1 test, already-active proven via exploding_event_appender), AC4 (4 cardinality tests + event-append-after-commit + error-propagation), AC5 (3 tests: permission-denial-before-read + both Keyword.fetch!/2 KeyError cases). Code reading confirmed the top-level rollback_definition_version/4 checks permission_checker strictly before calling do_rollback (the sole entry point to every Repo call in this feature), so the AC5 unprovisioned-but-decodable-schema-name mechanism genuinely proves ordering: a late permission check would hit the nonexistent Postgres schema first and raise/return {:transaction_failed,_} instead of cleanly {:error,:forbidden}. Code reading also confirmed AC3's already-active guard fires via Repo.rollback/1 inside run_rollback_transaction, before do_rollback ever calls finish_rollback (the only caller of event_appender) -- exploding_event_appender genuinely proves non-invocation, not just result shape. Event-append-after-commit test's reread_statuses_via_separate_connection/3 uses Task.async (a genuinely separate BEAM process/connection) combined with provisioned_tenant/0's explicit Ecto.Adapters.SQL.Sandbox.mode(Letflow.Repo, :auto) -- real commits, no wrapping transaction, matching store_test.exs's/promotion_test.exs's already-established working pattern -- so this is a real independent re-read, not the same sandboxed connection silently reusing TX1's transaction.

Ran mix test test/letflow/definitions/rollback_test.exs: 18 passed (matches TEST-DESIGNER's claim exactly). Ran full mix test: 647 passed (4 properties, 643 tests) -- matches claimed baseline+18 exactly, zero regressions.

Mutation-style sanity checks (both reverted cleanly, confirmed via git diff --stat producing no output afterward): (1) Reordered run_rollback_transaction/4's cond so the target-row lookup ran unconditionally before the current_active nil-check (simulating the exact reordering defect the guard-order describe block claims to catch) -- reran the file: 16/18 passed, and the 2 failures were precisely the 2 guard-order tests ('process_key_not_found wins' test crashed with {:transaction_failed, %BadMapError{}} instead of returning {:error,:process_key_not_found}; the 'zero rows' test flipped to {:error,:version_never_active}), proving the fixture genuinely disambiguates evaluation order, not merely asserts around it. (2) Changed supersede_matching_review/4's [_,_|_] ambiguous branch to blanket-supersede the first match instead of returning nil (reproducing the exact defect CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR's Rework 1 blocked on) -- reran the file: 17/18 passed, and the single failure was precisely the 'MORE THAN ONE matching row' test, confirming it genuinely catches a regression to blanket-supersede.

Grepped for @tag :skip, @tag :pending, TODO/FIXME, password/secret/connection-string patterns, Mox/mock/stub/meck in the test file: zero matches. Every fixture (two_version_history!/2, review_pending!/approved!/applied!/3) is built via real, already-merged public functions (Definitions.create/2/activate/2/deprecate/2/archive/2, PromotionReviewStore.insert_review/2/approve_review/4/mark_review_applied/2) -- no raw Repo.insert!/update_all bypassing a state machine anywhere in this file. Every test provisions its own tenant via provisioned_tenant/0 and uses unique_process_key/1 (System.unique_integer/1-suffixed) -- no shared/hardcoded identifiers, no cross-test dependency, no execution-order dependency, no wall-clock assertion. promotion_reviews fixtures use a fresh unique node id per sample_plan/2 call so plan_digest never collides on uq_promotion_review_active_digest even when two reviews target the same process_key (required for the ambiguous-match tests) -- confirmed correct by the passing 'MORE THAN ONE matching row' test itself. This is a WF-02 test-design gate, not a WF-03 regression test, so the pre-fix-failure confirmation requirement does not apply.

All 9 TEST-DESIGN-VALIDATOR checklist items (docs/agents/workflows/WF-02_requirement_implementation.md Step 3b) satisfied. No gaps found. PASS.
